claim: DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair by homologous recombination (HR) is thought to be restricted to the S- and G2- phases of the cell cycle in part due to 53BP1 antagonizing DNA end resection in G1-phase and non-cycling quiescent (G0) cells.
source: DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair by homologous recombination (HR) is thought to be restricted to the S- and G2- phases of the cell cycle in part due to 53BP1 antagonizing DNA end resection in G1-phase and non-cycling quiescent (G0) cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about cell cycle-dependent DSB repair and the role of 53BP1.

claim: LIN37, a component of the DREAM transcriptional repressor, functions in a 53BP1-independent manner to prevent DNA end resection and HR in G0 cells.
source: Here, we show that LIN37, a component of the DREAM transcriptional repressor, functions in a 53BP1-independent manner to prevent DNA end resection and HR in G0 cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by multiple experimental approaches including genetic epistasis analysis and chromatin-bound RPA assays.

claim: Loss of LIN37 leads to the expression of HR proteins, including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, and RAD51 in G0 cells.
source: Loss of LIN37 leads to the expression of HR proteins, including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, and RAD51, and promotes DNA end resection in G0 cells even in the presence of 53BP1.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data and western blot analysis showing increased expression of these proteins in LIN37-deficient cells.

claim: Loss of LIN37 promotes DNA end resection in G0 cells even in the presence of 53BP1.
source: Loss of LIN37 leads to the expression of HR proteins, including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, and RAD51, and promotes DNA end resection in G0 cells even in the presence of 53BP1.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing RPA accumulation at DSBs and End-seq data showing DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient cells.

claim: DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient G0 cells depends on BRCA1.
source: In contrast to 53BP1-deficiency, DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient G0 cells depends on BRCA1 and leads to RAD51 filament formation and HR.
evidence: This is supported by bulk gene inactivation experiments showing that loss of BRCA1 prevents RPA accumulation in LIN37-deficient cells.

claim: DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient G0 cells leads to RAD51 filament formation.
source: In contrast to 53BP1-deficiency, DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient G0 cells depends on BRCA1 and leads to RAD51 filament formation and HR.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing increased RAD51 foci in LIN37-deficient cells after IR.

claim: DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient G0 cells leads to homologous recombination.
source: In contrast to 53BP1-deficiency, DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient G0 cells depends on BRCA1 and leads to RAD51 filament formation and HR.
evidence: This is supported by the DR-GFP reporter assay showing increased HR-mediated DSB repair in LIN37-deficient cells.

claim: LIN37 is not required to protect DNA ends in cycling cells at G1-phase.
source: LIN37 is not required to protect DNA ends in cycling cells at G1-phase.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing minimal RPA accumulation in G1-phase LIN37-deficient cells compared to 53BP1-deficient cells.

claim: LIN37 regulates a novel 53BP1-independent cell phase-specific DNA end protection pathway that functions uniquely in quiescent cells.
source: Thus, LIN37 regulates a novel 53BP1-independent cell phase-specific DNA end protection pathway that functions uniquely in quiescent cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments showing LIN37 function is specific to G0 cells and independent of 53BP1.

claim: HR functions in the S- and G2-phases of the cell cycle using the sister chromatid as a template for precise homology-directed repair of DSBs.
source: HR functions in the S- and G2-phases of the cell cycle using the sister chromatid as a template for precise homology-directed repair of DSBs.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about HR mechanism and cell cycle regulation.

claim: NHEJ functions in all phases of the cell cycle to rejoin broken DNA ends.
source: In contrast, NHEJ functions in all phases of the cell cycle to rejoin broken DNA ends and is the only pathway of DSB repair in G1-phase cells and in non-cycling cells that have exited the cell cycle and are quiescent in G0, which comprise the majority of cells in the human body (Chang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature on NHEJ function.

claim: NHEJ is the only pathway of DSB repair in G1-phase cells and in non-cycling cells that have exited the cell cycle and are quiescent in G0.
source: In contrast, NHEJ functions in all phases of the cell cycle to rejoin broken DNA ends and is the only pathway of DSB repair in G1-phase cells and in non-cycling cells that have exited the cell cycle and are quiescent in G0, which comprise the majority of cells in the human body (Chang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: Quiescent G0 cells comprise the majority of cells in the human body.
source: In contrast, NHEJ functions in all phases of the cell cycle to rejoin broken DNA ends and is the only pathway of DSB repair in G1-phase cells and in non-cycling cells that have exited the cell cycle and are quiescent in G0, which comprise the majority of cells in the human body (Chang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: The initiation of HR requires DNA end resection to generate extended single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) overhangs that are coated by the trimeric ssDNA binding protein complex RPA1/2/3.
source: The initiation of HR requires DNA end resection to generate extended singlestranded DNA (ssDNA) overhangs that are coated by the trimeric ssDNA binding protein complex RPA1/2/3 (hereafter referred to as RPA) (Ciccia and Elledge, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature on HR mechanism.

claim: RPA is subsequently replaced by RAD51, and the RAD51 nucleofilament mediates a search for a homologous template usually within the sister chromatid to enable the completion of HR-mediated DNA DSB repair.
source: RPA is subsequently replaced by RAD51, and the RAD51 nucleofilament mediates a search for a homologous template usually within the sister chromatid to enable the completion of HR-mediated DNA DSB repair (Mimitou and Symington, 2009; Wyman et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on HR mechanism.

claim: NHEJ works best on DNA ends with minimal ssDNA overhangs, necessitating that DNA end resection be limited in G1-phase and G0 cells.
source: In contrast, NHEJ works best on DNA ends with minimal ssDNA overhangs, necessitating that DNA end resection be limited in G1-phase and G0 cells (Chang et al., 2017; Symington and Gautier, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on NHEJ mechanism.

claim: Extensive resection and ssDNA generation at broken DNA ends in cells at G0/G1 would antagonize NHEJ-mediated DSB repair and promote aberrant homology-mediated repair, forming chromosomal translocations and deletions leading to genome instability.
source: Extensive resection and ssDNA generation at broken DNA ends in cells at G0/G1 would antagonize NHEJ-mediated DSB repair and promote aberrant homology-mediated repair, due to the absence of sister chromatids, forming chromosomal translocations and deletions leading to genome instability (Ciccia and Elledge, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature and logical inference about consequences of inappropriate DNA end resection.

claim: The generation of ssDNA at broken DNA ends is the critical decision point for whether a DSB will be repaired by NHEJ and HR.
source: Therefore, the generation of ssDNA at broken DNA ends is the critical decision point for whether a DSB will be repaired by NHEJ and HR.
evidence: This is an inference based on the preceding discussion of HR and NHEJ mechanisms.

claim: BRCA1 initiates the resection of broken DNA ends with the CtIP and MRE11 nucleases generating short ssDNA tracts that are extended by other nucleases such as EXO1 and DNA2-BLM.
source: During HR, BRCA1 initiates the resection of broken DNA ends with the CtIP and MRE11 nucleases generating short ssDNA tracts that are extended by other nucleases such as EXO1 and DNA2-BLM (Symington and Gautier, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature on DNA end resection mechanism.

claim: Fanconia anemia (FA) proteins such as FANCD2 are involved in regulating DNA end resection.
source: Other proteins, including Fanconia anemia (FA) proteins such as FANCD2, are also involved in regulating DNA end resection (Unno et al., 2014; Murina et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: 53BP1 and its downstream effectors RIF1 and the shieldin complex antagonize DNA end resection in cells where NHEJ must repair DSBs.
source: In cells where NHEJ must repair DSBs, the extensive resection of DNA ends must be prevented and 53BP1 and its downstream effectors RIF1 and the shieldin complex antagonize DNA end resection in these cells (Setiaputra and Durocher, 2019; Mirman and de Lange, 2020; Bunting et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on 53BP1 pathway.

claim: 53BP1 and shieldin may protect DNA ends by inhibiting the recruitment or activity of pro-resection proteins and also by promoting DNA synthesis at resected DNA ends to 'fill in' the ssDNA gap generated by resection.
source: 53BP1 and shieldin may protect DNA ends by inhibiting the recruitment or activity of pro-resection proteins and also by promoting DNA synthesis at resected DNA ends to 'fill in' the ssDNA gap generated by resection (Mirman and de Lange, 2020; Setiaputra and Durocher, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature discussing potential mechanisms of 53BP1 function.

claim: Murine pre-B cells transformed with the Abelson murine leukemia virus kinase are rapidly cycling cells.
source: Murine pre-B cells transformed with the Abelson murine leukemia virus kinase, hereafter referred to as abl pre-B cells, are rapidly cycling cells (Rosenberg et al., 1975).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: When treated with the abl kinase inhibitor, imatinib, abl pre-B cells stop cycling with a predominantly 2N DNA content indicative of them being in G0/G1.
source: When treated with the abl kinase inhibitor, imatinib, abl pre-B cells stop cycling with a predominantly 2N DNA content indicative of them being in G0/G1 (Bredemeyer et al., 2006; Muljo and Schlissel, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: DNA DSBs in G0/G1 cells are repaired by NHEJ, which requires DNA Ligase 4 to join the broken DNA ends.
source: DNA DSBs in G0/G1 cells are repaired by NHEJ, which requires DNA Ligase 4 to join the broken DNA ends (Chang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature on NHEJ mechanism.

claim: DNA DSBs generated in non-cycling DNA Ligase 4-deficient (Lig4−/−) abl pre-B cells persist un-repaired.
source: Consequently, DNA DSBs generated in non-cycling DNA Ligase 4-deficient (Lig4−/−) abl pre-B cells persist un-repaired (Helmink et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: Persistent DSBs in non-cycling Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells are protected from nucleolytic activity and exhibit minimal DNA end resection.
source: These persistent DSBs are protected from nucleolytic activity and exhibit minimal DNA end resection (Tubbs et al., 2014; Dorsett et al., 2014; Helmink et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Loss of H2AX or 53BP1 in abl pre-B cells leads to extensive DNA end resection and the generation of ssDNA overhangs.
source: However, loss of H2AX or 53BP1 in abl pre-B cells leads to extensive DNA end resection and the generation of ssDNA overhangs (Tubbs et al., 2014; Dorsett et al., 2014; Helmink et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: ssDNA at resected DNA ends binds to RPA, which can be assayed by flow cytometry after detergent extraction of soluble RPA.
source: ssDNA at resected DNA ends binds to RPA, which can be assayed by flow cytometry after detergent extraction of soluble RPA (Forment et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established methodology.

claim: The generation of DSBs by ionizing radiation (IR) in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells led to robust chromatin-associated RPA as assayed by flow cytometry.
source: Indeed, as compared to non-cycling Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells, the generation of DSBs by ionizing radiation (IR) in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells led to robust chromatin-associated RPA as assayed by flow cytometry (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Multiple gRNAs to genes encoding proteins known to prevent DNA end resection such as 53BP1, RIF1, and shieldin subunits were enriched in the RPA-high cell population.
source: Multiple gRNAs to genes encoding proteins known to prevent DNA end resection such as 53BP1, RIF1, and shieldin subunits were enriched in the RPA-high cell population, demonstrating the veracity of this screening approach (Figure 1D and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the CRISPR screen data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Several gRNAs to Lin37, a gene encoding the LIN37 subunit of the MuvB complex, were highly enriched in RPA-high cells.
source: In addition, several gRNAs to Lin37, a gene encoding the LIN37 subunit of the MuvB complex, were also highly enriched in RPA-high cells (Figure 1D and Figure 1—source data 1; Litovchick et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by the CRISPR screen data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The MuvB complex forms the DREAM transcription repressor complex when bound to the pocket proteins p130/p107, and E2F proteins E2F4/5 and DP.
source: When bound to the pocket proteins p130/p107, and E2F proteins E2F4/5 and DP, the MuvB complex forms the DREAM transcription repressor complex, which functions to repress genes that promote entry into the cell cycle (Litovchick et al., 2007; Sadasivam and DeCaprio, 2013; Mages et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on DREAM complex.

claim: The DREAM transcription repressor complex functions to repress genes that promote entry into the cell cycle.
source: When bound to the pocket proteins p130/p107, and E2F proteins E2F4/5 and DP, the MuvB complex forms the DREAM transcription repressor complex, which functions to repress genes that promote entry into the cell cycle (Litovchick et al., 2007; Sadasivam and DeCaprio, 2013; Mages et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on DREAM complex function.

claim: LIN37-deficient cells exhibited increased RPA association with DSBs in chromatin after IR, with most of the cells lacking LIN37 having even more chromatin-bound RPA after IR than cells lacking 53BP1.
source: Similar to 53BP1-deficient abl pre-B cells, LIN37-deficient cells also exhibited increased RPA association with DSBs in chromatin after IR, with most of the cells lacking LIN37 having even more chromatin-bound RPA after IR than cells lacking 53BP1 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Increased RPA association at DSBs in LIN37-deficient cells is not a consequence of increased IR-induced DNA damage in the absence of LIN37.
source: This is not a consequence of increased IR-induced DNA damage in the absence of LIN37, because all the cells had similar levels of γH2AX indicative of similar DNA DSB generation in response to IR (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by γH2AX flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: RPA binding at DSBs in 53BP1 and LIN37 deficient abl pre-B cells does not depend on DNA Ligase 4 deficiency.
source: Analyses of non-cycling wild type (WT), Trp53bp1−/−, and Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells that expressed Ligase 4 yielded similar results, indicating that RPA binding at DSBs in 53BP1 and LIN37 deficient abl pre-B cells does not depend on DNA Ligase 4 deficiency (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: After irradiation, RPA phosphorylation at serine 4 and serine 8 of the RPA32 subunit was detected at higher levels in non-dividing Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− as compared to Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells.
source: After irradiation, RPA phosphorylation at serine 4 and serine 8 of the RPA32 subunit was also detected at higher levels in non-dividing Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− as compared to Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells, further suggesting that this RPA binding is at resected DNA ends (Figure 2C; Maréchal and Zou, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2C and citation to literature on RPA phosphorylation.

claim: Loss of LIN37 does not cause imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells to enter S-phase.
source: However, loss of LIN37 does not cause imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells to enter S-phase as evidenced by imatinib-treated Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells having primarily 2N DNA content and not incorporating BrdU, which is indicative of DNA synthesis in S-phase cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing DNA content and BrdU incorporation in Figure 2D.

claim: Chromatin-bound RPA in IR treated non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells formed discrete nuclear foci indicative of localization at DSBs.
source: Indeed, chromatin-bound RPA in IR treated non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells formed discrete nuclear foci indicative of localization at DSBs (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Non-cycling Lin37−/− and Trp53bp1−/− MCF10A cells exhibited increased chromatin-bound RPA after IR as compared to WT MCF10A cells.
source: Non-cycling Lin37−/− and Trp53bp1−/− MCF10A cells also exhibited increased chromatin-bound RPA after IR as compared to WT MCF10A cells (Figure 2H and I), indicating that the function of LIN37 in suppressing RPA accumulation at DNA DSBs in non-cycling cells is conserved in human and mouse.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2H and I.

claim: The function of LIN37 in suppressing RPA accumulation at DNA DSBs in non-cycling cells is conserved in human and mouse.
source: Non-cycling Lin37−/− and Trp53bp1−/− MCF10A cells also exhibited increased chromatin-bound RPA after IR as compared to WT MCF10A cells (Figure 2H and I), indicating that the function of LIN37 in suppressing RPA accumulation at DNA DSBs in non-cycling cells is conserved in human and mouse.
evidence: This is an inference based on data from both mouse and human cells showing similar phenotypes.

claim: The extent of RPA accumulation in human cells lacking LIN37 after IR was greater than seen in cells lacking 53BP1.
source: As was seen above in murine cells, the extent of RPA accumulation in human cells lacking LIN37 after IR was greater than seen in cells lacking 53BP1, suggesting that LIN37 plays an important role in preventing DNA end resection and extensive generation of ssDNA at DSBs in non-cycling mammalian cells (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2H and I.

claim: The CtIP nuclease is required to initiate DNA end resection during HR.
source: The CtIP nuclease is required to initiate DNA end resection during HR and DNA ends in non-cycling abl pre-B cells that are deficient in H2AX undergo resection that depends on CtIP (Sartori et al., 2007; Helmink et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on CtIP function.

claim: DNA ends in non-cycling abl pre-B cells that are deficient in H2AX undergo resection that depends on CtIP.
source: The CtIP nuclease is required to initiate DNA end resection during HR and DNA ends in non-cycling abl pre-B cells that are deficient in H2AX undergo resection that depends on CtIP (Sartori et al., 2007; Helmink et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The chromatin-bound RPA in IR treated non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− and Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells depended on CtIP.
source: The chromatin-bound RPA in IR treated non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− and Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells depended on CtIP (Figure 3A), indicating that the increased level of chromatin-bound RPA after IR in cells lacking LIN37 or 53BP1 is due to DNA end resection that would lead to the generation of ssDNA.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data after CtIP depletion shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The increased level of chromatin-bound RPA after IR in cells lacking LIN37 or 53BP1 is due to DNA end resection that would lead to the generation of ssDNA.
source: The chromatin-bound RPA in IR treated non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− and Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells depended on CtIP (Figure 3A), indicating that the increased level of chromatin-bound RPA after IR in cells lacking LIN37 or 53BP1 is due to DNA end resection that would lead to the generation of ssDNA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the CtIP-dependence of RPA accumulation.

claim: AsiSI DSBs in non-cycling Lig4−/−:iAsiSI abl pre-B cells were minimally resected (<200 bp).
source: The End-seq analysis revealed that while AsiSI DSBs in non-cycling Lig4−/−:iAsiSI abl pre-B cells were minimally resected (<200 bp), those in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/−:iAsiSI abl pre-B cells were resected up to 2 kb (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by End-seq data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: AsiSI DSBs in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/−:iAsiSI abl pre-B cells were resected up to 2 kb.
source: The End-seq analysis revealed that while AsiSI DSBs in non-cycling Lig4−/−:iAsiSI abl pre-B cells were minimally resected (<200 bp), those in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/−:iAsiSI abl pre-B cells were resected up to 2 kb (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by End-seq data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Loss of LIN37 leads to the CtIP-dependent resection of broken DNA ends in non-cycling cells.
source: We conclude that loss of LIN37 leads to the CtIP-dependent resection of broken DNA ends in non-cycling cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CtIP-dependence and End-seq data.

claim: CDK-dependent phosphorylation of CtIP is required to promote DNA end resection in cycling cells.
source: CDK-dependent phosphorylation of CtIP is required to promote DNA end resection in cycling cells (Huertas and Jackson, 2009; Huertas et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on CtIP regulation.

claim: Palbociclib treatment of imatinib-treated non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− and Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells did not affect the levels of chromatin-bound RPA after IR.
source: Palbociclib treatment of imatinib-treated non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− and Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells did not affect the levels of chromatin-bound RPA after IR, indicating CtIP-dependent resection in non-cycling cells does not require CDK4/6 activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CtIP-dependent resection in non-cycling cells does not require CDK4/6 activity.
source: Palbociclib treatment of imatinib-treated non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− and Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells did not affect the levels of chromatin-bound RPA after IR, indicating CtIP-dependent resection in non-cycling cells does not require CDK4/6 activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect of Palbociclib on RPA accumulation.

claim: Loss of LIN37 did not lead to reduction in the levels of 53BP1, RIF1, or SHLD1 proteins in cycling or non-cycling abl pre-B cells.
source: In this regard, western blot analysis revealed that loss of LIN37 did not lead to reduction in the levels of 53BP1, RIF1, or SHLD1 proteins in cycling or non-cycling abl pre-B cells (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: After IR treatment, robust and near equivalent numbers of 53BP1 and RIF1 foci form in non-cycling Lig4−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells.
source: Moreover, after IR treatment, robust and near equivalent numbers of 53BP1 and RIF1 foci form in non-cycling Lig4−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells, demonstrating that both 53BP1 and RIF1 efficiently localize to DSBs in LIN37-deficient cells (Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Both 53BP1 and RIF1 efficiently localize to DSBs in LIN37-deficient cells.
source: Moreover, after IR treatment, robust and near equivalent numbers of 53BP1 and RIF1 foci form in non-cycling Lig4−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells, demonstrating that both 53BP1 and RIF1 efficiently localize to DSBs in LIN37-deficient cells (Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the foci formation data.

claim: Loss of LIN37 in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells led to an increase in chromatin-bound RPA after IR, as compared to non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells that express LIN37.
source: Loss of LIN37 in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells led to an increase in chromatin-bound RPA after IR, as compared to non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells that express LIN37 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The loss of 53BP1 in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells led to increased chromatin-bound RPA after IR.
source: Similarly, the loss of 53BP1 in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells also led to increased chromatin-bound RPA after IR (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: In non-cycling cells 53BP1 and LIN37 are part of mechanistically distinct pathways that are both required to protect DNA ends from resection.
source: Given the additive effect of inactivation of both LIN37 and 53BP1, we conclude that in non-cycling cells 53BP1 and LIN37 are part of mechanistically distinct pathways that are both required to protect DNA ends from resection.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the epistasis analysis showing additive effects.

claim: LIN37 participates in the formation of the DREAM transcriptional repressor.
source: As LIN37 participates in the formation of the DREAM transcriptional repressor, we considered the possibility that LIN37 may protect DNA ends through the suppression of genes encoding pro-resection proteins (Sadasivam and DeCaprio, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature on DREAM complex.

claim: A mutant form of LIN37, LIN37CD, does not associate with the DREAM complex.
source: A mutant form of LIN37, LIN37CD, does not associate with the DREAM complex and while DREAM lacking LIN37 binds to its target genes, it cannot repress their expression (Mages et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature on LIN37 mutants.

claim: DREAM lacking LIN37 binds to its target genes, but cannot repress their expression.
source: A mutant form of LIN37, LIN37CD, does not associate with the DREAM complex and while DREAM lacking LIN37 binds to its target genes, it cannot repress their expression (Mages et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: Expression of WT LIN37, but not LIN37CD, in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells decreased IR-induced chromatin-bound RPA.
source: Expression of WT LIN37, but not LIN37CD, in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells decreased IR-induced chromatin-bound RPA (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: LIN37 functions to protect DNA ends through its activity in the DREAM transcriptional repressor.
source: That DNA end protection in LIN37-deficient cells can be restored by WT LIN37, but not LIN37CD, suggests that LIN37 functions to protect DNA ends through its activity in the DREAM transcriptional repressor.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential rescue by WT vs mutant LIN37.

claim: Cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells exhibit very few (approximately 20) significant gene expression changes as compared to Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells.
source: Cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells exhibit very few (approximately 20) significant gene expression changes as compared to Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: Non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells exhibited increased expression (>2-fold) of over 300 genes compared to non-cycling Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells.
source: In contrast, when compared to non-cycling Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells, non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells exhibited increased expression (>2-fold) of over 300 genes (Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Many genes upregulated in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells have functions in HR, including DNA end resection (Brca1, Bard1, Blm, and Exo1), recombination (Brca2, Bard1, Palb2, Mms22l, Rad51, Rad51b, and Rad54b), and DNA synthesis (Hrob/BC030867, Mcm3, Mcm4, Mcm5, Mcm7, Mcm8, Pold1, and Pole).
source: We found that many genes upregulated in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells have functions in HR, including DNA end resection (Brca1, Bard1, Blm, and Exo1), recombination (Brca2, Bard1, Palb2, Mms22l, Rad51, Rad51b, and Rad54b), and DNA synthesis (Hrob/BC030867, Mcm3, Mcm4, Mcm5, Mcm7, Mcm8, Pold1, and Pole).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: A subset of FA genes exhibited increased expression in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells.
source: A subset of FA genes also exhibited increased expression in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells (Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Many of the upregulated genes in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells were found to be bound by DREAM in NIH3T3 cells.
source: Many of the upregulated genes we identified were also found to be bound by DREAM in NIH3T3 cells (Figure 5—source data 1; Mages et al., 2017; Litovchick et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published DREAM binding data.

claim: The upregulated genes in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells are enriched in biological processes, such as cell cycle, cell division, DNA metabolic process, and DNA repair.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis reveals that the upregulated genes in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells are enriched in biological processes, such as cell cycle, cell division, DNA metabolic process, and DNA repair, consistent with previous analyses in LIN37-deficient mouse cells or human cells deficient in other DREAM components (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 5—source data 1; Mages et al., 2017; Litovchick et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and citations to previous studies.

claim: The levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, RAD51, and FANCD2 proteins were extremely low in non-cycling Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells compared to cycling cells.
source: Western blot analysis revealed that the levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, RAD51, and FANCD2 proteins were extremely low in non-cycling Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells compared to cycling cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The protein levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, RAD51, and FANCD2 were significantly elevated in non-cycling Lin37−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells as compared to WT and Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells, respectively.
source: Consistent with their increased transcript levels, the protein levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, RAD51, and FANCD2 were significantly elevated in non-cycling Lin37−/− and Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells as compared to WT and Lig4−/− abl pre-B cells, respectively (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Loss of LIN37 did not alter the levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, RAD51, and FANCD2 proteins in cycling cells.
source: In contrast, the levels of these proteins were not altered in cycling LIN37-deficient cells (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The increased expression of HR proteins was observed in non-cycling, but not cycling, Lin37−/− human MCF10A cells.
source: The increased expression of these HR proteins was also observed in non-cycling, but not cycling, Lin37−/− human MCF10A cells, indicating that LIN37 represses the expression of key DNA end resection and HR proteins to potentially limit DNA end resection in both human and murine non-cycling cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: LIN37 represses the expression of key DNA end resection and HR proteins to potentially limit DNA end resection in both human and murine non-cycling cells.
source: The increased expression of these HR proteins was also observed in non-cycling, but not cycling, Lin37−/− human MCF10A cells, indicating that LIN37 represses the expression of key DNA end resection and HR proteins to potentially limit DNA end resection in both human and murine non-cycling cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the conservation of the phenotype across species.

claim: The ability of LIN37 to repress the expression of key HR proteins in non-cycling cells requires LIN37 to function in the context of the DREAM complex.
source: The ability of LIN37 to repress the expression of these key HR proteins in non-cycling cells requires LIN37 to function in the context of the DREAM complex as evidenced by our observation that the expression of WT LIN37, but not LIN37CD in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells, led to a decrease in the levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, RAD51, and FANCD2 proteins (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5E comparing WT and mutant LIN37.

claim: The expression of the MRE11 and CtIP nucleases were not affected by the loss of LIN37 in cycling or non-cycling cells.
source: Of note is that the expression of the MRE11 and CtIP nucleases were not affected by the loss of LIN37 in cycling or non-cycling cells (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In non-cycling cells, LIN37, as part of the DREAM transcriptional repressor complex, represses genes encoding many proteins that function in DNA end resection and DSB repair by HR.
source: We conclude that in non-cycling cells, LIN37, as part of the DREAM transcriptional repressor complex, represses genes encoding many proteins that function in DNA end resection and DSB repair by HR.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on RNA-Seq and protein expression data.

claim: gRNAs to Rbbp8 (encodes CtIP) and to Mre11b (encodes MRE11) were enriched in RPA low cells from the reverse genetic screen.
source: As expected, gRNAs to Rbbp8 (encodes CtIP) and to Mre11b (encodes MRE11) were enriched in these RPA low cells, in agreement with their nucleolytic roles in resection and emphasizing the validity of our screen (Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the reverse genetic screen data.

claim: gRNAs to many genes encoding DNA end resection and HR proteins that are normally repressed by LIN37, including Brca1, Bard1, Blm, and several FA genes, were enriched in RPA low cells.
source: In addition, we isolated gRNAs to many genes encoding DNA end resection and HR proteins that are normally repressed by LIN37, including Brca1, Bard1, Blm, and several FA genes, indicating that the expression of these proteins brought about by LIN37-deficiency in non-cycling cells promotes the extensive DNA end resection that is observed in these cells (Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the reverse genetic screen data.

claim: The expression of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, and FANCD2 proteins brought about by LIN37-deficiency in non-cycling cells promotes the extensive DNA end resection that is observed in these cells.
source: In addition, we isolated gRNAs to many genes encoding DNA end resection and HR proteins that are normally repressed by LIN37, including Brca1, Bard1, Blm, and several FA genes, indicating that the expression of these proteins brought about by LIN37-deficiency in non-cycling cells promotes the extensive DNA end resection that is observed in these cells (Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the reverse genetic screen results.

claim: Bulk inactivation of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, or FANCD2 significantly reduced the level of chromatin-bound RPA after IR in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells.
source: Indeed, bulk inactivation of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, or FANCD2 significantly reduced the level of chromatin-bound RPA after IR in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl pre-B cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The loss of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, or FANCD2 had no effect on RPA localization to DSBs after IR treatment of non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells.
source: In striking contrast, the loss of these proteins had no effect on RPA localization to DSBs after IR treatment of non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells, further emphasizing that LIN37 and 53BP1 are part of mechanistically distinct pathways that prevent DNA end resection and ssDNA generation in non-cycling cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: LIN37 and 53BP1 are part of mechanistically distinct pathways that prevent DNA end resection and ssDNA generation in non-cycling cells.
source: In striking contrast, the loss of these proteins had no effect on RPA localization to DSBs after IR treatment of non-cycling Lig4−/−:Trp53bp1−/− abl pre-B cells, further emphasizing that LIN37 and 53BP1 are part of mechanistically distinct pathways that prevent DNA end resection and ssDNA generation in non-cycling cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential requirements for BRCA1 in the two pathways.

claim: LIN37-deficient non-cycling abl pre-B cells exhibited induction of Brca2, Palb2, and Rad51, which function to replace RPA with RAD51 on ssDNA to form RAD51 nucleofilaments at DSBs during HR.
source: LIN37-deficient non-cycling abl pre-B cells also exhibited induction of Brca2, Palb2, and Rad51, which function to replace RPA with RAD51 on ssDNA to form RAD51 nucleofilaments at DSBs during HR (Figure 5B, C and D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq and western blot data, along with established knowledge of these proteins' functions.

claim: There was a significant increase in the number of RAD51 foci in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl-pre-B cells after IR as compared to Lig4−/− abl-pre-B cells.
source: Indeed, there was a significant increase in the number of RAD51 foci in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl-pre-B cells after IR as compared to Lig4−/− abl-pre-B cells (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: There was an increase in homology-mediated DSB repair in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl-pre-B cells as compared to Lig4−/− abl-pre-B cells.
source: Indeed, using the HPRT-DR-GFP reporter for DSB repair by HR, we observed an increase in homology-mediated DSB repair in non-cycling Lig4−/−:Lin37−/− abl-pre-B cells as compared to Lig4−/− abl-pre-B cells (Figure 6C; Pierce et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by the DR-GFP reporter assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: In the absence of LIN37, the extensive DNA end resection can lead to HR-mediated DSB repair in non-cycling cells in the presence of 53BP1.
source: We conclude that in the absence of LIN37, the extensive DNA end resection can lead to HR-mediated DSB repair in non-cycling cells. Moreover, this occurs in the presence of 53BP1.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RAD51 foci and DR-GFP reporter data.

claim: Non-cycling imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells and EGF-deprived MCF10A cells had low levels of CDK4 and phospho-CDK4 indicative of them being in G0.
source: Both non-cycling abl pre-B cells and MCF10A cells had low levels of CDK4 and phsopho-CDK4 indicative of them being in G0 (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Phospho-Rb was not detected by western blot analysis of imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells or MCF10A cells deprived of EGF indicating that these cells are in G0.
source: Phospho-Rb was not detected by western blot analysis of imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells or MCF10A cells deprived of EGF indicating that these cells are in G0 (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: PCNA was not detected in imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells or MCF10A cells deprived of EGF.
source: PCNA, which is expressed early in the transition from G1 to S was also not detected in these cells (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells and MCF10A cells deprived of EGF have exited the cell cycle and entered G0, also known as quiescence.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells and MCF10A cells deprived of EGF have exited the cell cycle and entered G0, also known as quiescence, and LIN37 is required to protect DNA ends from resection in these cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on multiple cell cycle markers.

claim: LIN37 is required to protect DNA ends from resection in quiescent G0 cells.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that imatinib-treated abl pre-B cells and MCF10A cells deprived of EGF have exited the cell cycle and entered G0, also known as quiescence, and LIN37 is required to protect DNA ends from resection in these cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the characterization of the cell cycle state and the resection phenotype.

claim: G1-phase cells isolated from cycling populations expressed readily detectable levels of the HR proteins BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, FANCD2, and RAD51.
source: However, western blot analysis revealed that in contrast to G0 cells, G1 cells expressed readily detectable levels of the HR proteins BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, FANCD2, and RAD51.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data from sorted G1 cells.

claim: Loss of LIN37 did not lead to a significant change in the levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, FANCD2, and RAD51 proteins in G1-phase cells isolated from proliferating populations.
source: Moreover, loss of LIN37 did not lead to a significant change in the levels of these proteins in G1-phase cells isolated from proliferating populations (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7C and D.

claim: LIN37-DREAM functions to negatively regulate the expression of a subset of HR genes in G1-phase cells, however, this does not lead to a significant decrease in the levels of proteins encoded by these genes.
source: These results indicate that LIN37-DREAM functions to negatively regulate the expression of a subset of HR genes in G1-phase cells, however, this does not lead to a significant decrease in the levels of proteins encoded by these genes.
evidence: This is an inference based on RNA-Seq and protein expression data from G1 cells.

claim: G1 cells appear to depend primarily on 53BP1 for DNA end protection as evidenced by the substantial increase in RPA association with chromatin in IR treated 53BP1-deficient G1-phase cells as compared to LIN37-deficient G1-phase cells.
source: In contrast to G0 cells, which are dependent on 53BP1 and LIN37 for DNA end protection, G1 cells appear to depend primarily on 53BP1 as evidenced by the substantial increase in RPA association with chromatin in IR treated 53BP1-deficient G1-phase cells as compared to LIN37-deficient G1-phase cells (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: LIN37 functions to prevent DNA end resection primarily in quiescent G0 cells while 53BP1 functions in both proliferating G1 and quiescent G0 phase cells.
source: We conclude that LIN37 functions to prevent DNA end resection primarily in quiescent G0 cells while 53BP1 functions in both proliferating G1 and quiescent G0 phase cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparing RPA accumulation in G0 vs G1 cells.

claim: Rb and the DREAM complex are transcriptional repressors that silence the expression of genes required to promote cell cycle, driving cells to exit the cell cycle and enter G0 or quiescence.
source: Rb and the DREAM complex are transcriptional repressors that silence the expression of genes required to promote cell cycle, driving cells to exit the cell cycle and enter G0 or quiescence, where most cells in the human body reside (Mages et al., 2017; Weinberg, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on Rb and DREAM function.

claim: Most cells in the human body reside in G0 or quiescence.
source: Rb and the DREAM complex are transcriptional repressors that silence the expression of genes required to promote cell cycle, driving cells to exit the cell cycle and enter G0 or quiescence, where most cells in the human body reside (Mages et al., 2017; Weinberg, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Quiescent G0 cells and cycling cells in G1-phase have 2N DNA content and rely on NHEJ to repair DNA DSBs and maintain genome stability.
source: Quiescent G0 cells and cycling cells in G1-phase have 2N DNA content and rely on NHEJ to repair DNA DSBs and maintain genome stability.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell cycle and DNA repair.

claim: 53BP1 and its downstream effectors are required to promote NHEJ in G0 and G1 cells by antagonizing DNA end resection and ssDNA generation.
source: 53BP1 and its downstream effectors are required to promote NHEJ in G0 and G1 cells by antagonizing DNA end resection and ssDNA generation (Mirman and de Lange, 2020; Setiaputra and Durocher, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: In G0 cells, DNA end protection requires LIN37, a component of the DREAM complex.
source: However, here, we show that in G0 cells, DNA end protection also requires LIN37, a component of the DREAM complex.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: LIN37 function prevents aberrant homology-mediated joining in G0 cells.
source: Moreover, LIN37 function also prevents aberrant homology-mediated joining in G0 cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on the DR-GFP reporter assay.

claim: LIN37 association with DREAM is required for its transcriptional repressor function, but is not required for the binding of the complex to its target genes.
source: LIN37 association with DREAM is required for its transcriptional repressor function, but is not required for the binding of the complex to its target genes (Mages et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: DREAM complex binding sequences, termed cell cycle genes homology regions (CHRs), are found in the promoter regions of many HR genes.
source: In addition to genes encoding proteins that promote cell cycle, DREAM complex binding sequences, termed cell cycle genes homology regions (CHRs), are also found in the promoter regions of many HR genes (Mages et al., 2017; Müller et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Loss of LIN37 in G0 cells leads to the expression of many HR genes that promote DNA end resection such as Brca1, Bard1, Blm, and Fancd2.
source: Loss of LIN37 in G0 cells leads to the expression of many HR genes that promote DNA end resection such as Brca1, Bard1, Blm, and Fancd2 (Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data.

claim: Increased gene expression of HR genes in LIN37-deficient G0 cells leads to a significant increase in the levels of these proteins.
source: Moreover, this increased gene expression leads to a significant increase in the levels of these proteins in G0 cells (Figure 5C and D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data.

claim: Loss of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, or FANCD2 in LIN37-deficient G0 cells prevents DNA end resection.
source: Loss of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, or FANCD2 in LIN37-deficient G0 cells prevents DNA end resection demonstrating that the function of each of these proteins is required to promote DNA end resection in these cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data after bulk gene inactivation.

claim: The function of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, and FANCD2 is required to promote DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient G0 cells.
source: Loss of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, or FANCD2 in LIN37-deficient G0 cells prevents DNA end resection demonstrating that the function of each of these proteins is required to promote DNA end resection in these cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the rescue of the resection phenotype upon loss of these proteins.

claim: The expression of WT LIN37 in LIN37-deficient G0 cells prevents the expression of HR genes and DNA end resection.
source: Finally, while the expression of WT LIN37 in LIN37-deficient G0 cells prevents the expression of HR genes and DNA end resection the expression of LIN37CD, which cannot participate in forming a functional DREAM repressor complex, does not (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The expression of LIN37CD, which cannot participate in forming a functional DREAM repressor complex, does not prevent the expression of HR genes and DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient G0 cells.
source: Finally, while the expression of WT LIN37 in LIN37-deficient G0 cells prevents the expression of HR genes and DNA end resection the expression of LIN37CD, which cannot participate in forming a functional DREAM repressor complex, does not (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: LIN37-DREAM and 53BP1 function in distinct ways to protect DNA ends from aberrant resection.
source: LIN37-DREAM and 53BP1 function in distinct ways to protect DNA ends from aberrant resection.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on epistasis analysis and differential protein requirements.

claim: Resection in G0 LIN37-deficient cells relies on BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, and FANCD2.
source: Resection in G0 LIN37-deficient cells relies on BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, and FANCD2 as evidenced by the lack of DNA end resection in LIN37-deficient cells that have lost expression of any of these proteins (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data after bulk gene inactivation.

claim: 53BP1-deficient G0 cells express low levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, and FANCD2.
source: In contrast, 53BP1-deficient G0 cells express low levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, and FANCD2 and loss of expression of these proteins does not impact DNA end resection in these cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Loss of expression of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, and FANCD2 does not impact DNA end resection in 53BP1-deficient G0 cells.
source: In contrast, 53BP1-deficient G0 cells express low levels of BRCA1, BARD1, BLM, and FANCD2 and loss of expression of these proteins does not impact DNA end resection in these cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In G0 cells LIN37 prevents BRCA1-dependent DNA end resection whereas 53BP1 protects DNA ends from BRCA1-independent resection pathways.
source: Thus, in G0 cells LIN37 prevents BRCA1-dependent DNA end resection whereas 53BP1 protects DNA ends from BRCA1-independent resection pathways.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the differential requirements for BRCA1 in the two pathways.

claim: In G1-phase cells, 53BP1-RIF1 prevents BRCA1-CtIP from associating with DSBs and promoting resection.
source: In G1-phase cells, 53BP1-RIF1 prevents BRCA1-CtIP from associating with DSBs and promoting resection (Escribano-Díaz et al., 2013; Chapman et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: In S/G2-phase cells, BRCA1 inhibits RIF1 association with DSBs, which would otherwise antagonize resection.
source: In contrast, in S/G2-phase cells, this regulatory balance is tipped with BRCA1 inhibiting RIF1 association with DSBs, which would otherwise antagonize resection (Escribano-Díaz et al., 2013; Chapman et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: In G0 cells 53BP1 functions to protect DNA ends from resection.
source: Like G1-phase cells, in G0 cells 53BP1 functions to protect DNA ends from resection.
evidence: This is supported by the data showing RPA accumulation in 53BP1-deficient G0 cells.

claim: Upon the loss of LIN37 in G0 cells, the expression of HR proteins, including BRCA1, does not inactivate the 53BP1 pathway.
source: Upon the loss of LIN37 in G0 cells, the expression of HR proteins, including BRCA1, does not inactivate the 53BP1 pathway.
evidence: This is supported by the observation of 53BP1-RIF1 foci in LIN37-deficient cells.

claim: There is robust 53BP1-RIF1 association with DSBs in LIN37-deficient G0 cells.
source: Indeed, we find robust 53BP1-RIF1 association with DSBs in LIN37-deficient G0 cells and the loss of 53BP1 in these cells leads to increased RPA association at DSBs indicating that 53BP1 functions in DNA end protection in these cells (Figure 4B–E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and flow cytometry data.

claim: The loss of 53BP1 in LIN37-deficient G0 cells leads to increased RPA association at DSBs indicating that 53BP1 functions in DNA end protection in these cells.
source: Indeed, we find robust 53BP1-RIF1 association with DSBs in LIN37-deficient G0 cells and the loss of 53BP1 in these cells leads to increased RPA association at DSBs indicating that 53BP1 functions in DNA end protection in these cells (Figure 4B–E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the epistasis analysis.

claim: The genetic program activated by the loss of LIN37 in G0 cells leads to the activation of pathways that regulate the balance of anti-resection 53BP1 activities and pro-resection BRCA1 activities in a manner that favors DNA end resection.
source: We speculate that the genetic program activated by the loss of LIN37 in G0 cells leads to the activation of pathways that regulate the balance of anti-resection 53BP1 activities and pro-resection BRCA1 activities in a manner that favors DNA end resection.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism.

claim: These pathways do not prevent 53BP1-RIF1 association at DSBs in G0 cells.
source: Although the identity of these pathways and the manner in which they function is unknown, we show that they do not prevent 53BP1-RIF1 association at DSBs in G0 cells (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: LIN37-DREAM has additional activities in promoting genome stability by preventing resected DNA ends from progressing in HR-mediated DSB repair.
source: While LIN37-DREAM and 53BP1 both inhibit DNA end resection in G0 cells, LIN37-DREAM has additional activities in promoting genome stability by preventing resected DNA ends from progressing in HR-mediated DSB repair.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of RAD51 foci and HR activity in LIN37-deficient cells.

claim: LIN37-deficient G0 cells express BRCA2, PALB2, and RAD51 that convert RPA-coated ssDNA at broken DNA ends to RAD51 nucleofilaments that can mediate homology-mediated repair.
source: LIN37-deficient G0 cells express BRCA2, PALB2, and RAD51 that convert RPA-coated ssDNA at broken DNA ends to RAD51 nucleofilaments that can mediate homology-mediated repair (Figures 5B–D, 6B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), which in G0 cells could lead to aberrant homology-mediated DNA end joining.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq, western blot, immunofluorescence, and DR-GFP reporter data.

claim: Homology-mediated repair in G0 cells could lead to aberrant homology-mediated DNA end joining.
source: LIN37-deficient G0 cells express BRCA2, PALB2, and RAD51 that convert RPA-coated ssDNA at broken DNA ends to RAD51 nucleofilaments that can mediate homology-mediated repair (Figures 5B–D, 6B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), which in G0 cells could lead to aberrant homology-mediated DNA end joining.
evidence: This is speculation based on the absence of sister chromatids in G0 cells.

claim: Loss of LIN37-DREAM would not lead to a general defect in NHEJ-mediated DSB repair in G0 cells, which would be expected to occur rapidly before the broken DNA ends can be resected.
source: We speculate that loss of LIN37-DREAM would not lead to a general defect in NHEJ-mediated DSB repair in G0 cells, which would be expected to occur rapidly before the broken DNA ends can be resected.
evidence: This is speculation about the consequences of LIN37 loss.

claim: LIN37-DREAM function would prevent rare DSBs that are not rapidly repaired from being resected preventing normal NHEJ and promoting aberrant homology-mediated joining that occur in the setting of activating HR in the absence of a homologous sister chromatid.
source: Rather, LIN37-DREAM function would prevent rare DSBs that are not rapidly repaired from being resected preventing normal NHEJ and promoting aberrant homology-mediated joining that occur in the setting of activating HR in the absence of a homologous sister chromatid.
evidence: This is speculation about the role of LIN37-DREAM.

claim: Aberrant homology-mediated joining in G0 cells could result in chromosomal deletions, inversions, and translocations, common types of chromosomal rearrangements.
source: In this case, the homology would be found on the same or another chromosome leading to chromosomal deletions, inversions, and translocations, common types of chromosomal rearrangements.
evidence: This is speculation about potential consequences of aberrant HR in G0 cells.

claim: If resected DSBs in quiescent cells are repaired through 'allelic recombination' using homologous chromosomes as the repair templates during HR, this could result in loss of heterozygosity (LOH) of the chromosomes undergoing repair.
source: Additionally, if resected DSBs in quiescent cells are repaired through 'allelic recombination' using homologous chromosomes as the repair templates during HR, this could result in loss of heterozygosity (LOH) of the chromosomes undergoing repair.
evidence: This is speculation about potential consequences of HR in quiescent cells.

claim: LOH can cause loss of chromosomal region in the repaired chromosomes (LOH with copy number loss) or result in the replacement of WT, functional copy of genes with mutated, pathological genes on the homologous chromosomes (LOH with neutral copy number).
source: Depending on the homologous chromosomes serving as the repair templates, LOH can also cause loss of chromosomal region in the repaired chromosomes (LOH with copy number loss) or results in the replacement of WT, functional copy of genes with mutated, pathological genes on the homologous chromosomes (LOH with neutral copy number) (Bielas et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to literature on LOH mechanisms.

claim: In quiescent cells, LIN37-DREAM promotes genome stability by both antagonizing DNA end resection and preventing the aberrantly homology-mediated joining of resected DNA ends.
source: Thus, in quiescent cells, LIN37-DREAM promotes genome stability by both antagonizing DNA end resection and preventing the aberrantly homology-mediated joining of resected DNA ends.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the multiple functions of LIN37-DREAM demonstrated in the study.
